The HP-Report (dated 2014-02-21) section 第3-2(1)③ defines air as 79% nitrogen and 21% oxygen at 1 atm. Its worked examples compute nitrogen partial pressure as (100 + gauge kPa) × 0.79, which confirms adding atmospheric pressure to get absolute pressure. For this question: (100 + 300) × 0.79 = 316 kPa ≈ 0.31 MPa.

基発0109第2号 (dated 2015-01-09; the amendment took effect 2015-04-01, before the exam window) says nitrogen partial pressure exceeds 400 kPa above 0.4 MPa gauge. That also follows the absolute-pressure method.
Choice 1 (0.06 MPa), choice 2 (0.20), choice 3 (0.23, the gauge pressure alone × 0.79) and choice 5 (0.40, the total absolute pressure) all differ clearly from 0.316, so none is the closest value.
This is a physics calculation. It does not depend on which legal version was in force, and the amended rules were already in effect throughout the exam window.
